hints.title: In Place Value Sign Flagging
hints.text: The values in the array range from one to n. Each value corresponds directly to an index within the array. How can modifying signs mark presence without allocating extra space?

hints.title: Negative Marking Invariant
hints.text: For each number x, negating the value at index abs(x) minus one marks x as seen. Any index retaining a positive value was never visited.

hints.title: Sign Inversion Identification Procedure
hints.text: Iterate through the array. For each element, let target index be abs(x) minus one. If the element at target index is positive, make it negative. In a second pass, collect all index plus one values where the element remains strictly positive. Return the collected list.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Using hash sets or boolean arrays allocates O(N) extra space, violating the O(1) auxiliary space constraint.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place sign negation marks elements in O(N) time while using strictly O(1) auxiliary space beyond the output list.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle already negated values using abs() and restore original signs if in-place mutation must be reversible.
